# Source-Preserving BUET–Hamner Native Assembly

This provisional F07 calculation, issue #12157, constructs a separate native
OpenSim candidate by retaining the BUET upper extremities, trunk, pelvis,
femurs, and their 473 muscles, then appending eight Hamner distal-leg bodies,
eight joints, and 84 lower-limb muscles. It is an explicit source-ownership
decision rather than an anatomical merger inferred from names. The six Hamner
aggregate trunk muscles and two aggregate psoas muscles are excluded because
BUET owns the trunk and proximal region. BUET source psoas fascicles are not
asserted force-equivalent to the excluded Hamner aggregates. No donor source
field, muscle law, path, wrap, mass, frame, or joint is edited.

## Source, Frames, and State Domain

Recipe version one accepts only the reviewed BUET entrypoint XML SHA-256
`b66a31e08087327f8756d587f471b0494a3d9d6f7f6d510de66beba4a9e79bf6`
and Hamner XML SHA-256
`349ce7a44f1541794f2283cab73bb954270228f2f50808de549ec5097a1687cf`.
The sources and fresh output must be distinct paths. The assembly verifies
matching native pelvis/femur mass, center of mass and inertia, and the right
and left hip CustomJoint SpatialTransforms before cloning. The BUET model owns
the shared pelvis and femurs. Hamner supplies `tibia`, `talus`, `calcn`, and
`toes` on each side, with knee, ankle, subtalar and MTP joints. Cloning actual
native components retains their source frame/socket, path and wrap properties.
After serialization, a fresh OpenSim load compares each retained body, joint,
muscle and constraint native property dump to its source. No source file or
derived model is committed to the public repository; the hash-bound diagnostic
receipt is retained.

Native `initSystem` may assemble its initial state. The comparison uses three
declared common hip-coordinate poses: $(0,0,0)$, $(0.2,-0.1,0.15)$ and
$(-0.15,0.08,-0.12)$ radians for flexion/adduction/rotation on each side,
with corresponding speeds $(0.07,-0.03,0.02)$ rad/s. This is an explicitly
sampled common-coordinate check, not complete native-state or whole-motion
equivalence. The default BUET upper coordinates and source path active sets
are not exhaustively varied. Model coordinate, pelvis-frame, observation,
anatomical attachment, and private marker registration remain uncalibrated.

## Native Mechanical Comparison

For a retained body $i$, compare native ground transform $X_i(q)$ and spatial
velocity $V_i(q,u)$ against its owning source. For each retained muscle $j$,
compare native path length $\ell_j(q)$ and lengthening speed
$\dot\ell_j(q,u)$. The check covers three common poses and all 557 retained
muscles; it does not infer physiological muscle work or path power from those
two path observations. Native muscle/joint properties and all retained BUET
constraints are compared after a fresh XML reload.

The derived native mass matrix $M_d(q)$ must be finite and have positive
minimum eigenvalue at each sample. The diagnostic records the native total
applied generalized force

$$f_d=J_{\mathrm{system}}^\mathsf{T}F_{\mathrm{body}}+f_{\mathrm{mobility}},$$

reusing the source-bound zero-MTP native comparison authority. This force
includes body forces from gravity and muscles, not merely direct mobility
forces. It is not compared to a naive sum of two whole-model force vectors:
the sources overlap on pelvis/femurs, and added distal masses and muscles act
through those shared bodies. Inertial bias and constraint reactions remain
separate. Native QErr and UErr are observed at the sampled poses. Positive
mass and finite force are numerical diagnostics, not passive-force, balance,
contact or dynamic-equivalence admission.

## Executed Evidence and Remaining Gates

OpenSim `4.6-2026-06-22-85aaf64` with exact loaded native simulation, Simbody
and actuator binary hashes reloaded the 40-body, 557-muscle candidate. Three
native integration tests and four portable contract tests passed. Every
sampled retained transform, velocity, muscle length and path speed difference
was zero; sampled QErr/UErr was zero. The minimum native mass eigenvalue was
`1.3362969448668327e-06` in mixed native mobility units. The generalized
force vector norm was `54563.69711509691` in mixed native generalized units,
which must not be interpreted as a physiological force threshold. The exact
source/output/adapter and runtime hashes are in the F07 receipt and turnover.
Changed entrypoint XML bytes, an unreviewed digest and an existing output path
reject. Failed native verification removes its fresh output.

The XML hash covers the entrypoint artifact, not transitive visual resources;
source loading reported missing visual meshes. This candidate retains BUET
partial locked abdominal translations, couplers, conditional/moving path
points, wrap objects, and any source passive-load behavior. The separately
studied Abdjnt two-translation reduction and zero-MTP factory reduction are
distinct derived policies, not silent steps in this assembly. Active wrap
transitions, full-state and controller restart, source muscle physiology,
foot/club contact, model-specific passive calibration, complete native Moco
feasibility, matched golfer marker correspondence and independent full-horizon
excitation replay remain open. All 17 model variants and six engine families
remain in the required denominator. Canonical publication remains blocked.
